subject.title: TUI: Support Shift+Enter for newline (Enter to send)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public TUI send/newline keybinding preference, or only document the current dependency-backed Shift+Enter/Ctrl+J behavior and fallback?
rationale: The default newline behavior is already dependency-backed, but a configurable send/newline mode would create new public TUI config or CLI surface under the repo's high bar for configuration options.

options.title: Document Current Shortcuts First
options.body: Add docs and /help coverage for Shift+Enter, Ctrl+J, terminal limitations, and the backslash fallback, while deferring configurable keybindings until a settings owner is approved.

options.title: Add Scoped TUI Keybinding Preference
options.body: Approve a narrow config or CLI owner for send/newline keybindings and implement wiring, docs, and tests around that chosen public contract.

options.title: Close As Dependency-Covered
options.body: Treat the dependency-backed default as enough and close the remaining configurable-keybinding request without adding public config surface.

recommendation.title: Document Current Shortcuts First
recommendation.body: Add docs and /help coverage for Shift+Enter, Ctrl+J, terminal limitations, and the backslash fallback, while deferring configurable keybindings until a settings owner is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter previously reviewed this exact issue and has the strongest TUI wrapper/docs history for deciding the product boundary.
